chunks: And as for what was narrated: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and said to him, 'Inform me about the dowry of the woman that it is not permissible for the believers to exceed.' He said, 'The Prophetic Sunnah is five hundred dirhams. So whoever exceeds that, it is returned to the Sunnah, and there is no penalty upon him for more than five hundred dirhams. If he gives her from the five hundred dirhams one dirham or more of that, then he consummates the marriage with her, there is no penalty upon him.'

I said, 'And if he divorces her after he has consummated the marriage with her?' He said, 'She gets nothing. Her condition was only five hundred dirhams. So when he consummated the marriage with her before she completed her dowry, it demolished the dowry, so she gets nothing; she only has what she took before he consummated the marriage with her. So if she claims after that, while he is alive or after his death, she gets nothing.'

So the first thing in this report is that it was not narrated by anyone other than Muhammad ibn Sinan from Mufaddal ibn Umar, and Muhammad ibn Sinan is weak, very weak. And what he narrates exclusively, without anyone else sharing in it, is not acted upon. Then indeed the report includes that the dowry is not increased beyond five hundred dirhams, and whenever it is increased, it is returned to five hundred. And this also, we have previously presented the opposite of, that the dowry is whatever people agree upon, whether little or much.

key_terms.السُّنَّةُ الْمُحَمَّدِيَّةُ: The Prophetic Sunnah, referring to the established practice or standard amount
key_terms.دِرْهَم: A silver coin, used here as the unit of currency for the dowry
key_terms.مَطْعُونٌ عَلَيْهِ: Weak or flawed (referring to a narrator's reliability)
key_terms.مَهْر: Dowry or bridal gift given by the husband to the wife

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on exceeding the standard dowry amount and what happens to the excess if divorced after consummation?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* presents a specific juristic view that the 'Prophetic Sunnah' sets a ceiling of five hundred dirhams for the dowry (mahr), with excess amounts being forfeited if the wife is divorced after consummation but before full payment. The compiler, Shaykh al-Tusi, critiques this ruling by highlighting the weakness of the primary narrator, Muhammad ibn Sinan, and contrasts it with the dominant Shia position that mahr is determined by mutual agreement (taradhin) without a strict upper limit, thereby illustrating the methodological process of evaluating chain reliability against substantive legal principles.
